title: International Criminal Court issues arrest warrants for Putin and Lvova-Belova
body:
On 17 March 2023 the International Criminal Court (ICC) announced that Pre-Trial Chamber II had issued arrest warrants for Russian President Vladimir Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova, Russia's Presidential Commissioner for Children's Rights. The warrants were the first issued by the court in connection with the war in Ukraine.

Both were accused of the war crimes of unlawful deportation of population and unlawful transfer of population from occupied areas of Ukraine to the Russian Federation, specifically involving children. The charges fall under articles 8(2)(a)(vii) and 8(2)(b)(viii) of the Rome Statute, and the alleged conduct began in occupied Ukrainian territory at least from 24 February 2022. The chamber acted on an application by the ICC Prosecutor submitted in February 2023.

The court found Putin allegedly responsible for committing the acts directly, jointly with others or through others, and for failing to control subordinates who committed them. Lvova-Belova was alleged to be responsible for committing the acts directly, jointly or through others.

The warrants were initially issued under seal to protect victims, witnesses and the investigation. The court then made their existence public, stating that public awareness might help prevent further crimes. Neither Russia nor Ukraine is a state party to the Rome Statute. Ukraine has accepted the court's jurisdiction through ad hoc declarations, and Russia withdrew its signature from the statute in 2016.
